cards.title: Question Formation
rule: Definition: Question Formation & Interrogative Structures (ሕቶኣዊ መዋቕራትን ኣሰራርዓኦምን) refers to the syntactic rules governing the creation of direct and indirect questions, including yes/no questions, Wh-questions, subject vs. object questions, and embedded clauses, utilizing auxiliary inversion and precise word order.

English interrogative structures are fundamentally divided into direct questions ($$\text{Direct Questions}$$) and indirect or embedded questions ($$\text{Indirect Questions}$$). To signal a direct question, English strictly requires grammatical inversion, where the auxiliary verb is placed before the subject ($$\text{Auxiliary} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$), or the introduction of a dummy auxiliary. Tigrinya, conversely, forms yes/no questions synthetically by attaching the suffix particle "-ዶ" (do) directly to the inflected main verb (e.g., "መጺኡ" [he came] $$\rightarrow$$ "መጺኡዶ?" [did he come?]). It does not employ auxiliary inversion. Wh-questions in Tigrinya insert the question word directly into the standard declarative Subject-Object-Verb slot without modifying the word order (e.g., "ንስኻ ኣበይ ትነብር?" [Where do you live?]). Because Tigrinya lacks auxiliary inversion and dummy 'do'-support, students frequently make word order errors in direct English questions (e.g., writing "Where you are going?" instead of "Where *are you* going?").

examples.text: She goes to school every day.
She go to school every day.
examples.fix: She goes to school every day.

cards.title: Notes
body: Definition: Question Formation & Interrogative Structures (ሕቶኣዊ መዋቕራትን ኣሰራርዓኦምን) refers to the syntactic rules governing the creation of direct and indirect questions, including yes/no questions, Wh-questions, subject vs. object questions, and embedded clauses, utilizing auxiliary inversion and precise word order.

English interrogative structures are fundamentally divided into direct questions ($$\text{Direct Questions}$$) and indirect or embedded questions ($$\text{Indirect Questions}$$). To signal a direct question, English strictly requires grammatical inversion, where the auxiliary verb is placed before the subject ($$\text{Auxiliary} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$), or the introduction of a dummy auxiliary. Tigrinya, conversely, forms yes/no questions synthetically by attaching the suffix particle "-ዶ" (do) directly to the inflected main verb (e.g., "መጺኡ" [he came] $$\rightarrow$$ "መጺኡዶ?" [did he come?]). It does not employ auxiliary inversion. Wh-questions in Tigrinya insert the question word directly into the standard declarative Subject-Object-Verb slot without modifying the word order (e.g., "ንስኻ ኣበይ ትነብር?" [Where do you live?]). Because Tigrinya lacks auxiliary inversion and dummy 'do'-support, students frequently make word order errors in direct English questions (e.g., writing "Where you are going?" instead of "Where *are you* going?").

Direct Yes/No questions require the syntactic pattern $$\text{Auxiliary} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb} \dots ?$$. In the simple present and simple past tenses, where no auxiliary is naturally present in active declarative clauses, English inserts the dummy auxiliary "do" ($$\text{Do/Does/Did} + \text{Subject} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$). A common error on national exams is failing to return the main verb to its base form after using "do/does/did" (e.g., writing "Did she *went*?" instead of the correct "Did she *go*?"). Tigrinya speakers must remember that the tense marker is carried entirely by the auxiliary, leaving the main verb in its bare infinitive state.

cards.title: Form wh-questions about the subject and the object
cards.problem: Ask questions about the underlined words in "Samuel helped Ruth." (a) about Samuel, (b) about Ruth.

steps.text: **Step 1: Subject question – the wh-word replaces the subject, no auxiliary.** (a) Who helped Ruth?
**Step 2: Object question – wh-word + auxiliary + subject + base verb.** (b) Who(m) did Samuel help?
**Step 3: Check the verb form.** In (b) "did" carries the past, so the verb is base "help".
**Tip:** if the answer is the subject, do not add do/does/did.

cards.answer: (a) Who helped Ruth? (b) Who(m) did Samuel help?

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Could you please tell me what time ________ from the regional airport tomorrow morning?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is an indirect (embedded) question introduced by the polite phrase 'Could you please tell me'. It requires declarative word order: $$\text{Wh-word (what time)} + \text{Subject (the flight)} + \text{Verb (departs)}$$.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose Option A ('does the flight depart') or Option C ('will the flight depart') because they assume they need direct question inversion. However, indirect questions must not use auxiliary inversion or dummy do-support.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እዚ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ብ 'Could you please...' ዝጅምር ውሽጣዊ ሕቶ (Indirect/Embedded question) እዩ። ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ውሽጣዊ ሕቶታት ስርዓተ-ሕቶ (inversion) ኣይህልዎምን፤ ልክዕ ከም ስሩዕ ኣዎንታዊ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ($$Subject + Verb$$) እዮም ዝጸሓፉ። ስለዚ እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'the flight' ቅድሚ እቲ ግሲ 'departs' ክስራዕ ኣለዎ (Option B)። 'does the flight depart' ምጥቃም ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Why ________ your science project on time last Friday, as the teacher requested?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
This is a direct past Wh-question. It requires the past dummy auxiliary 'didn't' to precede the subject 'you', and the main verb must return to its base form: $$\text{Why} + \text{didn't} + \text{Subject} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Option A incorrectly combines 'didn't' with the past tense verb 'submitted'. Option B fails to invert the subject and auxiliary. Option C correctly uses 'didn't' with the base verb 'submit'.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ቀጥታዊ ሕሉፍ ሕቶ ክንሓትት ከለና እቲ ሓገዝቲ ግሲ ('didn't') ቅድሚ እቲ ዋና ባእታ ('you') ክስራዕ ኣለዎ። ከምኡ ውን 'did' ወይ 'didn't' ምስ ዝህልው፡ እቲ ቀንዲ ግሲ ወትሩ ናብቲ መበቆላዊ ቅጥዑ (base form - 'submit') ክምለስ ኣለዎ። ስለዚ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option C እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Past simple questions: Wh-word + did + subject + base verb.

**Step 2:** "put" is the base form (and irregular).

**Step 3:** So: Where did you put the keys?

**Tip:** Questions: (Wh-word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb. Subject questions (Who called?) have no auxiliary. Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.q: Could you please tell me what time ________ from the regional airport tomorrow morning?
questions.label: 1. Could you please tell me what time ________ from the regiona
why: This is an indirect (embedded) question introduced by the polite phrase 'Could you please tell me'. It requires declarative word order: $$\text{Wh-word (what time)} + \text{Subject (the flight)} + \text{Verb (departs)}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Why ________ your science project on time last Friday, as the teacher requested?
questions.label: 2. Why ________ your science project on time last Friday, as th
why: This is a direct past Wh-question. It requires the past dummy auxiliary 'didn't' to precede the subject 'you', and the main verb must return to its base form: $$\text{Why} + \text{didn't} + \text{Subject} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: ________ the rare historical manuscript from the library archive last week?
questions.label: 3. ________ the rare historical manuscript from the library arc
why: This is a subject question asking about the person who performed the action of stealing. In English subject questions, no auxiliary do-support ('did') is used, and the verb remains in its past simple form ($$\text{Who/What} + \text{V}_2 + \text{Object}$$
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: I wonder whether ________ ready to present their research findings to the board.
questions.label: 4. I wonder whether ________ ready to present their research fi
why: This is an embedded Yes/No question introduced by 'I wonder'. It requires the complementizer 'whether' followed by declarative word order: $$\text{whether} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: ________ were you talking to when the school director walked into the biology lab?
questions.label: 5. ________ were you talking to when the school director walked
why: The preposition 'to' is stranded at the end of the clause ('talking to'). In informal/standard English, when the preposition is stranded, the subjective pronoun 'Who' is used at the beginning of the question.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Can you tell me how long ________ as a teacher in this regional high school?
questions.label: 6. Can you tell me how long ________ as a teacher in this regio
why: This is an indirect question introduced by 'Can you tell me'. It requires declarative word order: $$\text{Wh-word (how long)} + \text{Subject (Aster)} + \text{Verb (has been working)}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: ________ did you invite to speak at the national graduation ceremony next month?
questions.label: 7. ________ did you invite to speak at the national graduation
why: This is an object question asking about the person receiving the invitation. In formal English, the objective pronoun 'Whom' is used when asking about the object of a verb.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Do you know ________ the main administrative office is temporarily closed today?
questions.label: 8. Do you know ________ the main administrative office is tempo
why: This is an indirect question introduced by 'Do you know'. It requires declarative word order, so the Wh-word 'why' must be followed directly by the subject 'the main administrative office'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: ________ of these two biology reference books do you recommend for the exam preparation?
questions.label: 9. ________ of these two biology reference books do you recomme
why: The question asks for a choice between a limited, specific group ('these two biology reference books'). This requires the selective question word 'Which'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: To ________ should I address this formal letter of application for the scholarship?
questions.label: 10. To ________ should I address this formal letter of applicati
why: The preposition 'To' is fronted to the beginning of the question. In formal English, a fronted preposition must strictly be followed by the objective pronoun 'whom': $$\text{Preposition} + \text{whom} \dots$$
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.label: 11. Why ____ your project on time last Friday?

Form a negative question: (you / come / why)

questions.label: 12. Who ____ the window?

similar.q: Ask about the subject: Someone called me.
Ask about the object: She called someone.

Subject questions use normal word order without "did".

questions.q: Could you tell me where ____?
questions.label: 13. Could you tell me where ____?

similar.a: Do you know what time it is?
Can you tell me where he works?

why: Answer D: the bus station is
"Could you tell me" makes an indirect question.
Indirect questions use statement order: subject + verb.
So: where the bus station is.
questions.tip: Questions: (Wh-word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb. Subject questions (Who called?) have no auxiliary. Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.q: Correct the error: "What you are doing?"
questions.label: 14. Correct the error: "What you are doing?"
why: Direct questions need inversion: auxiliary before subject.
questions.tip: Questions: (Wh-word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb. Subject questions (Who called?) have no auxiliary. Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.q: Choose the correct question for the answer: "I have lived here for five years."
questions.label: 15. Choose the correct question for the answer: "I have lived here for five years."

options.A: How long are you living here since?
options.B: How long have you lived here?
options.C: How long you have lived here?
options.D: How long did you lived here?

why: Answer B: How long have you lived here?
The answer uses the present perfect with "for".
The question asks about duration: How long + have + subject + past participle.
So: How long have you lived here?
questions.tip: Questions: (Wh-word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb. Subject questions (Who called?) have no auxiliary. Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.q: ____ do you go to the dentist? – Twice a year.
questions.label: 16. ____ do you go to the dentist? – Twice a year.
why: "Twice a year" answers a question about frequency.
"How long" asks about duration; "How far" about distance.
questions.tip: Questions: (Wh-word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb. Subject questions (Who called?) have no auxiliary. Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.q: Read: "Interviewer: ____? Athlete: I started running when I was nine, in my village near Mendefera." Which question fits?
questions.label: 17. Read: "Interviewer: ____? Athlete: I started running when I was nine, in my village near…

similar.q: Question for "Because I loved the feeling of freedom."
Question for "In my village near Mendefera."

why: Answer C: When did you start running?
The answer gives a time: "when I was nine".
A past time question: When did you start running?
The other options have wrong word order or do not match.
questions.tip: Questions: (Wh-word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb. Subject questions (Who called?) have no auxiliary. Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.q: ____ book is this? – It's Saba's.
questions.label: 18. ____ book is this? – It's Saba's.

similar.q: Complete: ____ (Whose / Who's) coming to the party?

questions.tip: Questions: (Wh-word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb. Subject questions (Who called?) have no auxiliary. Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.q: I wonder whether they ____ ready.
questions.label: 19. I wonder whether they ____ ready.

similar.q: Complete: I'm not sure if she ____ (can / can she) come.
Complete: Nobody knows where he ____ (has gone / has he gone).

why: After "I wonder whether", use statement order.
It is a statement, so no question mark.
questions.tip: Questions: (Wh-word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb. Subject questions (Who called?) have no auxiliary. Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.q: True or false: "Which of you knows the answer?" is a correct subject question.
questions.label: 20. True or false: "Which of you knows the answer?" is a correct subject question.
why: True. "Which of you" is the subject of "knows".
Subject questions use statement order without do/does.
